summary: Skagit County lookout site: camp in 1918, cupola cabin around 1922-23, fire detection to 1949 per USFS, collapsed under snow around 1965; ruins remain and Trail 640 reaches the site.

facts.design: 12-foot square wooden cabin with a 6-foot square cupola (1950 USGS description)
facts.status_note: Cabin collapsed under heavy snow in or around 1965; ruins remain on the summit

staffing.status: fire detection 1926 to 1949 per the Forest Service; a 1951 newspaper item has the lookout reporting a fire

access.note: Forest Service Trail 640 leads to the former lookout site; older WillhiteWeb directions describe a gated road

visit.trail_note: Forest Service Trail 640: the first mile climbs steeply up an old road; directions start from the Darrington Ranger District office and take Highway 530 west

events.note: Camp lookout set up (WillhiteWeb says the camp probably started about two years earlier)
Contract submitted to build a cab on the site (April 1920, per WillhiteWeb)
Cupola cabin replaced the camp, per the Former Fire Lookout Sites register and firelookout.com; other sources date completion to 1923
Construction of the cupola cabin completed in September 1923 (Forest Lookouts quoting a newspaper; WillhiteWeb)
Used for fire detection in the summers from 1926, per the Forest Service
Lookout reported a fire at an old slash burn; two trucks with 35 CCC men sent; the fire was then reported apparently out
Panoramic photos taken from the cupola (July 18, 1935)
Fire detection use ran through 1949, per the Forest Service
Forest Lookouts says abandoned in 1949; WillhiteWeb says abandoned at some point in the 1950s
August 1951 fire discovered and reported by the lookout (newspaper item quoted by Forest Lookouts and WillhiteWeb); later than the 1949 end date
Cabin destroyed by snow, or collapsed under heavy snow, in or around 1965

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Former Fire Lookout Sites register and firelookout.com say a cupola cabin replaced the camp in 1922. The Forest Lookouts page quotes a September 1923 notice that the new lookout house was completed, and WillhiteWeb says the construction finished in September 1923 after an April 1920 contract. The story gives both.

The Forest Service says fire detection ran from 1926 to 1949, and Forest Lookouts says the lookout was abandoned in 1949. A newspaper item quoted on Forest Lookouts and WillhiteWeb describes the lookout reporting an August 1951 fire, which is after 1949. The story reports both and does not settle it.

notes_for_editor: Dates for the cabin and the end of use conflict across sources; the story says so. The WillhiteWeb gated-road directions come from an older access section (the page cites a 1956 USGS survey and a 1977 update), so they may be out of date; the Forest Service trail page is the current reference. Firetower.org's cached page shows a 'Date Registered' label with no value, so the brief's 2012 FFLOS date was not verified. Wikipedia is used only for location.
